original_question: Let K be a non-polar compact subset of R, let μ_K be its equilibrium measure, and let P_n(x;μ_K) be the n-th monic orthogonal polynomial with zero set Z_n(μ_K)={x:P_n(x;μ_K)=0}. If U_n(μ_K)=inf{|x-x'|: x,x'∈Z_n(μ_K), x≠x'} denotes the minimal spacing between distinct zeros, determine whether there is a general relationship between this zero spacing and the smoothness of the Green function g_{C\K}; also determine whether there is a general relationship between that zero spacing and the Markov factors of K.
target_in_paper: §3 (Orthogonal polynomials), Problem 6: the open problem asking whether there is a general relation between the zero spacing of the orthogonal polynomials for the equilibrium measure μ_K of a non-polar compact set K⊂R and the smoothness of the Green function g_{C\K}, and likewise whether there is a relation between that zero spacing and the Markov factors of K.
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper's official formulation. It correctly identifies the ambient setting K⊂R with K non-polar, the use of the equilibrium measure μ_K, the monic orthogonal polynomials P_n(·;μ_K), the zero set Z_n(μ_K), the minimal zero spacing U_n(μ_K), and the two exact targets of the problem: possible relations with the smoothness of g_{C\K} and with the Markov factors of K. In fact, it essentially restates Problem 6, while adding the explicit definitions of Z_n and U_n that the paper gives immediately beforehand.
missing_details: To make the second clause fully stand-alone, the n-th Markov factor M_n(K) should be defined explicitly as the operator norm of differentiation on polynomials of degree at most n with the sup norm on K.
The Green function should be identified as the Green function of C\K with pole at infinity.

The nearby smoothness discussion in §2 assumes that K is regular with respect to the Dirichlet problem so that g_{C\K} extends continuously to K; this is implicit background when one speaks about smoothness near K.
The paper's question concerns the overall zero-spacing behavior, i.e. the sequence {U_n(μ_K)}_{n≥1}, rather than a single fixed n.
For complete self-containment, one should state that n ranges over positive integers and that the orthogonal polynomials are taken with respect to the probability Borel measure μ_K.
It is worth making explicit that the paper leaves 'general relation' qualitative; it does not prescribe a specific asymptotic law, modulus, or equivalence notion for Problem 6 itself.
refined_question: Let K⊂R be a non-polar compact set, let μ_K be the equilibrium measure of K, and for each n≥1 let P_n(x;μ_K) be the n-th monic orthogonal polynomial with respect to μ_K. Define Z_n(μ_K):={x∈R:P_n(x;μ_K)=0} and U_n(μ_K):=inf{|x-x'|:x,x'∈Z_n(μ_K), x≠x'}. Let g_{C\K} denote the Green function of C\K with pole at infinity, and let M_n(K) denote the n-th Markov factor, i.e. the operator norm of differentiation on polynomials of degree at most n equipped with the uniform norm on K. Assuming, when discussing smoothness near K, the regularity background used in §2, what general relationship, if any, exists between the zero-spacing sequence {U_n(μ_K)}_{n≥1} and the smoothness of g_{C\K} near K, and what general relationship, if any, exists between {U_n(μ_K)}_{n≥1} and the Markov factors {M_n(K)}_{n≥1}?
justification: The draft is targeting Problem 6, not any neighboring conjecture or theorem. The paper introduces the monic orthogonal polynomials in §1.1, introduces μ_K notation there as the equilibrium measure, defines Z_n(μ) and U_n(μ) immediately before Problem 6 in §3, and states Problem 6 almost exactly in the language used in the draft. The nearby context also explains why Markov factors are relevant (§2 defines M_n(K) and relates Green-function smoothness to Markov-type growth) and why regularity with respect to the Dirichlet problem is a hidden background assumption for smoothness questions about g_{C\K}. The motivating discussion just before Problem 6 uses the Cantor-type sets K(γ), where estimates for U_n(μ_{K(γ)}) and M_{2^s}(K(γ)) are compared, confirming that the draft is aimed at this precise open problem rather than a broader one.
